subject: How to custom label position in imsn()? What is the "convert to genclone" for ?

messages.author: fb72064169045944
messages.subject: How to custom label position in imsn()? What is the "convert to genclone" for ?
parts:
Hi, Thanks for all the help here firstly. And, I have new problems.  I have implemented imsn() for my data  , but I find the labels are so densely clumped and centered at the colored "circle". See the picture:

 I couldn't find how to adjust in the GUI, but I notice the codes are: 
Bly_snpclo_sub <- popsub(Bly_snpclo, blacklist = character(0))
Bly_snpclo_nomiss <- missingno(Bly_snpclo, type = 'mean')
Bly_snpclo_dist <- bitwise.dist(Bly_snpclo_nomiss, percent = TRUE, mat = FALSE, missing_match = TRUE, differences_only = FALSE, threads = 0)
min_span_net <- poppr.msn(Bly_snpclo_sub, Bly_snpclo_dist, showplot = FALSE, include.ties = TRUE)

set.seed(69)
plot_poppr_msn(Bly_snpclo,
               min_span_net,
               inds = "ALL",
               mlg = FALSE,
               gadj = 11,
               nodebase = 1.15,
               palette = rainbow,
               cutoff = NULL,
               quantiles = FALSE,
               beforecut = TRUE,
               layfun = igraph::layout_with_dh)

Is there a way to make the labels more separated and "off " the "circle" ? 

Additionally,  what is the "convert to a genclone ?" option in the GUI for ? If my data is already a snpclone object, is this process necessary ?

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] How to custom label position in imsn()? What is the "convert to genclone" for ?
parts: Is there a way to make the labels more separated and "off " the "circle" ?

Yes. You can add additional igraph plotting parameters as arguments to the plot_poppr_msn function. I would recommend using vertex.label.dist and/or vertex.label.degree (see the igraph documentation for details: http://igraph.org/r/doc/plot.common.html).
Additionally,  what is the "convert to a genclone ?" option in the GUI for ? If my data is already a snpclone object, is this process necessary ?

No, the process is not necessary if your data is already snpclone or genclone. In fact, you can ignore it since it does nothing if the incoming object already is a genclone/snpclone object. This option is meant for those who have genind or genlight objects. It offers a small speedup since the calculation of MLGs only has to be performed once for genclone/snpclone objects. 

Hope that helps,
Zhian

P.S. You may want to update to the new version of poppr so that the nodes in your MSN are scaled by area.
